prompt: What is the risk of writing the same lines in two environments' files?

choices.text: The files become too large for Git to diff
choices.why: Git diffs files far larger than these without trouble.

choices.text: Flux applies the shared lines twice
choices.why: Each file is applied by its own Kustomization, once.

choices.text: Kubernetes rejects identical objects in two namespaces
choices.why: Identical objects in different namespaces are normal.

choices.text: One copy gets changed and the other does not
choices.why: Right. Every line written twice is a line that will one day be changed once.

prompt: Which of these belong to Helm rather than Kustomize? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Every file valid YAML on its own
choices.why: Kustomize's promise; a template is not valid until rendered.

choices.text: A chart filled from values
choices.why: Right. Templates with holes, filled per installation.

choices.text: A release with a history
choices.why: Right. Helm tracks each installation and can roll it back.

choices.text: A base and its overlays
choices.why: That is Kustomize's vocabulary.

prompt: What does the base say about staging or production?

choices.text: Production's values, which staging overrides
choices.why: The base belongs to neither environment.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. No namespace, no tag, no message: it is what every environment shares.

choices.text: Their namespaces, so overlays can find them
choices.why: Each overlay sets its own namespace.

choices.text: Which of the two is promoted first
choices.why: Promotion order is a matter of pull requests, not of the base.

prompt: Why run kubectl diff -k before merging the conversion to Kustomize?

choices.text: The PR diff hides the effect
choices.why: Right. The rendered diff shows what will change in the cluster: a ConfigMap and one rollout.

choices.text: kubectl diff installs the overlay as a dry run
choices.why: It changes nothing in the cluster.

choices.text: Flux refuses overlays that were never diffed
choices.why: Flux applies what Git says; it keeps no record of diffs.

choices.text: Gitea requires it for files under apps/
choices.why: Gitea requires the validate status, nothing else.

prompt: Why does the new validate.sh write the build to a file instead of piping it to kubeconform?

choices.text: kubectl kustomize writes only to files
choices.why: It writes to standard output by default.

choices.text: So a failed build fails the check
choices.why: Right. A pipe would hand kubeconform nothing, and nothing validates.

choices.text: kubeconform cannot read from a pipe
choices.why: It reads standard input; the problem is an empty one.

choices.text: The file is kept as a record for the auditor
choices.why: It is deleted with the work directory.

prompt: validate.sh passes -skip ___ to kubeconform, because that kind's schema is Flux's and not Kubernetes'.
An overlay needs a different replica count. What should it use?

choices.text: A JSON patch on /spec/replicas
choices.why: It works, and says the mechanics instead of the intent.

choices.text: A second base with three replicas
choices.why: A second base is the duplication Kustomize exists to remove.

choices.text: A strategic merge patch with the whole Deployment
choices.why: That copies the base back into the overlay.

choices.text: The replicas field
choices.why: Right. A field Kustomize knows says the intent in one line.

prompt: Why is /spec/ports/0/nodePort fragile?

choices.text: It joins on a position in a list
choices.why: Right. A port added at the front would move the patch onto the wrong one, with no error.

choices.text: JSON patches cannot add fields
choices.why: add is one of the operations it uses.

choices.text: nodePort is not allowed in a base
choices.why: The base leaves it out; the overlay adds it.

choices.text: Kustomize applies JSON patches before the base
choices.why: Patches apply to the built base.

prompt: How does production's strategic merge patch put resources on the right container?

choices.text: By a target selector on the patch
choices.why: This patch has no target; it names its own object.

choices.text: By the image name
choices.why: Containers merge by name, not by image.

choices.text: By the container's position in the list
choices.why: That is how a JSON patch works, not a strategic merge.

choices.text: Containers are matched by name
choices.why: Right. The resources land on bulletin and nothing else moves.

prompt: Why does a change to a generated ConfigMap's literal roll the pods?

choices.text: A new hash renames it, which changes the pod template
choices.why: Right. Nothing has to remember to restart anything.

choices.text: Kubernetes restarts pods when any ConfigMap changes
choices.why: It does not, which is the trap the generator closes.

choices.text: Flux restarts every pod on every apply
choices.why: Flux applies; Kubernetes rolls only a changed template.

choices.text: The kubelet watches environment variables
choices.why: Environment variables are read once, at start.

prompt: What happened to staging's old ConfigMap after the new message was merged?

choices.text: Kept, for a rollback
choices.why: Git holds the old literal; the cluster does not keep the object.

choices.text: Left as an orphan for a person to delete
choices.why: Flux's prune removes it on the same pass.

choices.text: Renamed to the new hash
choices.why: A new object was created with the new name.

choices.text: Pruned
choices.why: Right. No file describes it any more.

prompt: Why does the lesson warn against secretGenerator literals?

choices.text: Flux refuses to apply Secrets
choices.why: Flux applies Secrets like any object.

choices.text: Secrets cannot have a hash suffix
choices.why: They get one exactly like ConfigMaps.

choices.text: They would be in Git in clear text
choices.why: Right. Lessons 9 and 10 bring secrets in other ways.

choices.text: secretGenerator only works in Helm
choices.why: It is a Kustomize generator.

prompt: What does helm template do?

choices.text: Creates a new chart skeleton
choices.why: That is helm create.

choices.text: Installs the chart as a release
choices.why: That is helm install, or Flux's helm controller.

choices.text: Renders it, offline
choices.why: Right. It is what a reviewer reads and a check validates.

choices.text: Uploads the chart to a registry
choices.why: That is helm push, lesson 7's subject.

prompt: Why can kubeconform not check charts/bulletin/templates directly?

choices.text: kubeconform only reads JSON
choices.why: It reads YAML; the templates are not valid YAML yet.

choices.text: The templates use a Kubernetes version kubeconform lacks
choices.why: The version is not the obstacle.

choices.text: Templates are not valid YAML until rendered
choices.why: Right. Render with helm template, then validate the output.

choices.text: Charts carry their own schemas that replace Kubernetes'
choices.why: A chart may carry a values schema, which is a different thing.

prompt: Inside a template, .Release.___ is the name the installation was given.
Why does helm list -n preview show the release that Flux installed?

choices.text: Argo CD registered it with Helm
choices.why: Argo CD is not in this cluster any more, and creates no releases.

choices.text: helm list reads Flux's HelmRelease objects
choices.why: It reads Helm's release Secrets.

choices.text: Flux copies its state into Helm after each sync
choices.why: There is nothing to copy: it uses Helm's own code and storage.

choices.text: Flux installs it as an ordinary Helm release
choices.why: Right. History and rollback work as with any release.

prompt: Where does Helm keep the record of a release?

choices.text: In Flux's source controller artifact
choices.why: The artifact holds the chart files, not releases.

choices.text: In a Secret in the release's namespace
choices.why: Right. That is what helm list and helm history read.

choices.text: In a file on your machine
choices.why: Nothing local is needed; any machine with access sees it.

choices.text: In the chart directory in fleet
choices.why: The chart is the source; the release is state in the cluster.

prompt: During an incident on an Argo CD-managed chart, why might helm rollback fail?

choices.text: Charts installed by Argo CD are read-only
choices.why: They are ordinary objects; there is just no release.

choices.text: Argo CD renders charts and makes no Helm release
choices.why: Right. There is no release for helm to roll back.

choices.text: helm rollback needs Flux installed
choices.why: Helm needs no Flux.

choices.text: Argo CD encrypts the release Secrets
choices.why: There are no release Secrets.

prompt: Match each case to the tool the lesson suggests.

pairs.left: Your team's own service, two environments
One change a third-party chart offers no value for

prompt: A team renders manifests in CI and commits the output for the agent to apply. What do they gain and pay?

choices.text: No need for a reviewer; more storage
choices.why: The point is to make review easier, not unnecessary.

choices.text: Encrypted secrets; a longer pipeline
choices.why: Rendering has nothing to do with secrets.

choices.text: A reviewer reads the final manifests, and a second copy falls out of step
choices.why: Right. That is the trade, and the default stays rendering in the agent.

choices.text: Faster syncs; no Helm releases
choices.why: Speed is not the gain, and releases are a separate matter.

prompt: helm template ran with --set message="Rendered, not installed." and the message came out as Rendered. Why?

choices.text: The quotes were wrong
choices.why: The shell passed the whole string; Helm split it.

choices.text: --set reads a comma as the start of the next key
choices.why: Right. Escape it as \, or use a values file.

choices.text: The chart truncates every message after its first word
choices.why: The chart prints whatever value it gets.

choices.text: helm template drops punctuation
choices.why: Nothing in Helm drops punctuation.

prompt: A patch's target names a Service that does not exist, through a typo. What does kubectl kustomize do?

choices.text: Refuses the whole build
choices.why: That would be safer, and it is not what happened.

choices.text: Builds anyway, with the patch applied to nothing
choices.why: Right. The Service came out without its nodePort, and nothing complained.

choices.text: Creates the missing Service
choices.why: Patches change objects; they never create the target.

choices.text: Applies the patch to the first Service it finds instead
choices.why: It matches by kind and name, and found none.

prompt: Which check would have caught the patch that matched nothing?

choices.text: kubeconform -strict
choices.why: The output was a valid Service; it passed.

choices.text: Gitea's required approval
choices.why: A reviewer might see it, but nothing guarantees they would.

choices.text: An assertion on the built output
choices.why: Right. Only a check that knows what staging should contain can see it.

choices.text: kubectl kustomize returning an error
choices.why: It returned none.

prompt: What does required in a chart template buy you?

choices.text: A default value when the user gives none
choices.why: required has no default; it refuses.

choices.text: An early, readable error
choices.why: Right. Without it the image would render as localhost:5001/bulletin: and fail in the cluster.

choices.text: A faster helm install
choices.why: It changes nothing about speed.

choices.text: Validation against Kubernetes schemas
choices.why: It checks that a value exists, not its schema.

prompt: Order what happened to the staging message change in this lesson.
items: A literal changes in the overlay
Flux applies a ConfigMap with a new hash
The pods roll and the old ConfigMap is pruned
trap: The build is checked before the merge, and the rollout follows the new name.

prompt: A third environment, qa, should run what staging runs with one replica. What is the smallest correct change?

choices.text: Copy staging's overlay and change the namespace only
choices.why: That leaves qa at three replicas, and copies the rest.

choices.text: A new overlay over the same base, and a file in clusters/lab/
choices.why: Right. The overlay holds qa's differences and nothing else.

choices.text: Add qa as a second namespace to staging's overlay
choices.why: An overlay has one namespace.

choices.text: A new base for qa
choices.why: The base is what all environments share; qa is one more overlay.

prompt: Which file in an overlay lists the base as a resource?

choices.text: namespace.yaml, next to it
choices.why: It only names the namespace.

choices.text: kustomization.yaml
choices.why: Right. resources names ../base.

choices.text: deployment.yaml
choices.why: The Deployment lives in the base.

choices.text: Chart.yaml
choices.why: That belongs to a Helm chart.

prompt: Why does kubectl diff use --field-manager=kustomize-controller?

choices.text: To let kubectl write to the cluster
choices.why: diff never writes.

choices.text: To compare as Flux applies
choices.why: Right. Otherwise your apply would change nothing Flux owns.

choices.text: Because kustomize-controller must approve the diff
choices.why: Nothing approves a diff.

choices.text: To make the diff run faster
choices.why: It changes ownership, not speed.

prompt: Why is /spec/ports/0/nodePort a fragile path to patch?

choices.text: nodePort is read-only
choices.why: It can be set.

choices.text: A port added at the front would move the patch onto it
choices.why: Right. Position is a weak join.

choices.text: JSON patches are deprecated
choices.why: They are fully supported.

choices.text: Service ports can only change by recreating the Service
choices.why: They can be patched, as the overlays do.

prompt: Why does a ConfigMap read at start need configMapGenerator to take effect?

choices.text: The new name changes the pod template
choices.why: Right. Otherwise pods keep the old values.

choices.text: The kubelet only mounts hashed names
choices.why: It mounts any ConfigMap.

choices.text: Kubernetes deletes plain ConfigMaps on change
choices.why: It updates them in place.

choices.text: Flux ignores ConfigMaps without a hash
choices.why: It applies them like anything else.

prompt: Which command checks a chart's structure without a cluster?

choices.text: helm history
choices.why: It shows a release's revisions.

choices.text: helm list
choices.why: It lists releases in a cluster.

choices.text: helm install
choices.why: It installs into a cluster.

choices.text: helm lint
choices.why: Right. The check to put in a chart's CI.

prompt: In a template, what is .Values?

choices.text: values.yaml plus the overrides
choices.why: Right. The installation's answers win.

choices.text: Only the chart's values.yaml
choices.why: Overrides are merged in.

choices.text: The Chart.yaml metadata
choices.why: That is .Chart.

choices.text: The live object's fields
choices.why: Templates never read the cluster.

prompt: Why should you know which tool installed a chart before typing helm rollback in an incident?

choices.text: helm rollback deletes the namespace
choices.why: It reverts to an earlier revision.

choices.text: helm rollback needs Gitea's approval
choices.why: Helm knows nothing about Gitea.

choices.text: Only Argo CD keeps a release history
choices.why: Flux's releases keep Helm's history.

choices.text: Only Flux makes real Helm releases
choices.why: Right. helm list shows nothing for Argo CD's.

prompt: Where does Helm store a release Flux installed?

choices.text: In the fleet repository
choices.why: Git holds the HelmRelease, not Helm's record.

choices.text: In the source controller's artifact for the chart
choices.why: That holds the chart, not the release.

choices.text: In a file on your laptop
choices.why: Nothing about it is on your laptop.

choices.text: In a Secret in the release's namespace
choices.why: Right. Where helm list finds it.

prompt: A third-party chart lacks a value for one change you need. What does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: Patch Helm's output with Kustomize
choices.why: Right. Flux's postRenderers and Argo CD both support it.

choices.text: Render it once and stop using Helm
choices.why: That throws away what the chart gives you.

choices.text: Fork the chart and maintain your copy
choices.why: That is a large cost for one change.

choices.text: Edit the live objects by hand
choices.why: The agent would undo it.

prompt: What does a build that succeeds prove?

choices.text: That the cluster will accept it
choices.why: Admission and quotas decide that later.

choices.text: That every patch matched
choices.why: A patch can match nothing silently.

choices.text: That the pods will be ready
choices.why: Readiness is decided in the cluster.

choices.text: That the files are well formed
choices.why: Right. Not that they say what you meant.
